title: A residual soft X-ray floor fits seven ASASSN-14ko cycles better than one fixed fractional dip
abstract: We test whether soft X-ray dips in ASASSN-14ko remove one fixed fraction of the flux or a variable component above a residual floor. Fixed coverage rules admit 69 Swift visits in seven cycles of 2020-2024, including two faint cycles. A negative-binomial count model with a common floor beats a common fractional dip by 14.29 in AIC. An affine model leaves 5.6 percent of the variable component after the dip, with a bootstrap 97.5th percentile of 12.0 percent. A complete switch to a floor remains adequate. The model difference vanishes when the two faint cycles are removed. Fits to 14 window totals retain the floor preference. The result quantifies state-dependent visibility of the X-ray clock and gives a count-noise exposure rule. It does not measure a new period, identify the floor with a specific nucleus, or explain the period stall. The bootstrap assumes independent negative-binomial fluctuations and is not a test against arbitrary correlated AGN noise.

display.caption: Seven cycles meet the coverage rule. A shared residual level fits the soft counts better than one fractional loss. Error bars include count noise only; likelihood fits also include intrinsic scatter.
